summary: P2-A UserNotificationBell E2E frontend verification: ALL 7 acceptance criteria PASS. Logged in as test@aurem.dev on preview URL, landed on /dashboard, bell rendered in TopBar (ds2-topbar) at top-right, badge showed exactly '2' (matches the 2 seeded unread rows — no stale extras). Opened panel, both seeded notifications present newest-first (ship_failed first, scan_done second). ship_failed row: data-persistent='true' + amber AlertTriangle icon. scan_done row: data-persistent='false' + no warning icon. 'Mark all read' button visible; clicking it made badge vanish, items remained (2 still listed) but visually dimmed via opacity-60 class and data-unread flipped to 'false'. Escape closes panel. Page reload: badge stays gone, items still present with data-unread='false' — proves real backend round-trip via GET /notifications + POST /notifications/read-all. Outside click also closes panel. TopBar regression: no layout overlap/breakage, project switcher breadcrumb still renders next to the new bell. Live badge count observed: 2.
critical_code_review_comments: UserNotificationBell.jsx: markOne error path is silently swallowed (.catch(()=>{})) — consider surfacing a toast on failure so users know their read-click didn't persist. Same for markAll and refresh. Non-blocking for P2-A.

Amber AlertTriangle icon only renders when `n.persistent && !n.read_at`. After 'Mark all read', persistent items lose their amber flag visually — this matches the spec ('marked read, not removed') and passed testing, but confirm with product whether persistent-but-read items should still keep a subtle amber accent for scannability.
Polling every 30s + on-open is fine for now, but consider server-sent-events / websocket push in a follow-up so persistent events (payment_failed / ship_failed) surface faster than 30s worst-case.
Console during dashboard load shows one 401 (unauth request pre-hydration) and later a 403 + 404 from unrelated endpoints — not caused by the bell. Worth a lightweight cleanup in a separate ticket.
